newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Democrats slam Republican tax cut plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Democrats slam Republican tax cut plan.

text.p: Senate Democrats Wednesday charged that a nearly $200 billion five-year tax cut put forward by Republicans would increase the budget deficit from $121 billion in fiscal 1997 to $251 billion in 2002.

A report compiled for the minority Democrats on the Senate Budget Committee criticized Republicans for offering their tax cut proposal without specifying how it would be paid to avoid increasing the deficit.
"Providing tax cuts of this magnitude would require extreme cuts in programs that are critical to middle class Americans," the report said.

The estimated $251 billion deficit was calculated by the Congressional Budget Office for Sen. Frank Lautenberg, the senior Democrat on the Budget Committee. The estimate assumed no action was taken to offset the tax cuts with spending cuts or tax hikes in other areas.
Republicans announced their tax cut proposal in January. However, action on tax cuts has been held up pending the start of negotiations on a balanced budget.

Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, R-New Mexico, said earlier this week a $70 billion five-year tax cut, offset by equal tax hikes as suggested by President Clinton, would be the maximum possible unless other changes in federal spending were approved.

The Republican tax proposal announced in January includes a child tax credit of $500 for children up to age 18, a reduction in the capital gains tax rate paid on investment profits, and a reduction in the estate tax.
Clinton has proposed a $98 billion five-year tax cut which includes a smaller child tax credit. It would be partially paid for with $76 billion in tax increases in other areas of the economy.
